title: The Thanksgiving massacre you’ve never heard of… The De La Roche Family Murders
tags: get ready with me and makeup
description:
A quiet Thanksgiving weekend in 1976. A picture-perfect New Jersey family of five. And by sunrise… there is only one survivor.

When 18-year-old Harry De La Roche Jr. flagged down police screaming that his whole family was dead, it kicked off one of the most twisted, confusing, and hotly debated murder cases in New Jersey history. I'm talking... conflicting stories, missing pieces, a confession that may... or may not... be real, and a family dynamic that was anything but normal.

Was Harry a cold-blooded killer? A kid pushed past his breaking point? Or the lone survivor of something even darker?

Today we’re diving into the De La Roche murders, a case filled with questions that, even 45 years later, still don’t have clear answers.

Im just saying, it can be legal for someone to confess without their Miranda rights being read, because Miranda warnings are only required for custodial interrogations meaning AFTER  you’re under arrest; voluntary statements or confessions made during informal questioning, can be used in court, but a confession during a true custodial interrogation without the warning might be inadmissible if challenged, though the case isn't automatically dismissed. 

At that point Harry had not been arrested he was voluntarily giving the information. At the age of 18 he didn’t have to have representation unless he asked for it and didn’t have to have his Aunt/Uncle there. 

Should he have gotten rest before the polygraph test? Yes
